person.shortBio: Full Stack & Systems Engineer at Fountane specializing in Next.js, Go microservices, and enterprise AI orchestration. Engineered a zero-trust AI orchestrator resolving queries across 600+ microservice endpoints with sub-100ms routing latency and strict tenant isolation.
longBio: I'm a software engineer from India. I started building for the web while studying Computer Applications at Patna University, contributed to open source with Real Dev Squad, and joined Fountane in August 2024 as a Junior Full Stack Developer, advancing to Associate Full Stack Developer.

Day to day I engineer scalable systems across Next.js and Go: high-density UI modules, transactional backend services, payment gateways, and role-based access control. I build and maintain zero-trust AI agent orchestration layers that query multi-service backends under strict tenant isolation.
Outside code I ride. I have ridden solo from Patna to Ladakh and from Patna to Rameshwaram, documenting the roads, mechanics, and lessons on a dedicated Rides section.

rides._note: Powers the separate /rides page with its own look. Fill the nulls with real values. Do not guess distances or dates.

page.title: On Two Wheels
page.tagline: Patna to the edge of the map, and back.
page.intro: When I'm not shipping code, I'm on a motorcycle. These are my long solo rides: the routes, the stories, the telemetry, and what the road taught me.

rides.title: Bangalore to Patna (Northbound Return)
rides.summary: The grand return leg heading north across Karnataka, Telangana, Hyderabad, Jabalpur, and the Gangetic plains back home to Patna.
rides.story: Northbound trans-subcontinent return run connecting Bangalore through central India back to Patna basecamp.
highlights: Completing the 10,000+ km southern touring circuit back at Patna basecamp.
lessons: Consistent 80-90 km/h cruising preserves tire life and rider stamina over multi-day legs.

rides.title: Bangalore to Nandi Hills & Adiyogi
rides.summary: Early morning mountain climb up Nandi Hills switchbacks followed by the highway run to Adiyogi Chikkaballapura and return to Bangalore.
rides.story: Chasing the sunrise above the cloud line at Nandi Hills before rolling through the Chikkaballapura granite landscape to the Adiyogi monument.
highlights: Sunrise cloud sea above the Nandi Hills cliff curves.
Cruising the scenic Chikkaballapura rural highways to Adiyogi.
lessons: Early dawn starts reward you with empty switchbacks and cool engine temps.

rides.title: Kolli Hills: 70 Hairpin Bends
rides.summary: The ultimate detour on the Bangalore–Rameshwaram expedition: conquering all 70 continuous numbered hairpin bends of Kolli Malai up and down in one non-stop push.
rides.story: 140 hairpin bends in a single morning assault — scaling the sheer wall of Kolli Hills to Solakkadu summit, turning right around, and carving back down before hammering south toward Rameshwaram.
highlights: Scaled all 70 numbered hairpin bends up to Solakkadu summit at 1,300m elevation.
Turned around at the top and carved all 70 bends downhill back to the base in one continuous push (140 hairpins total).
Mastered 2nd-gear apex carving and steep-gradient engine braking without brake fade on the Meteor 350.
Rejoined NH44 south toward Madurai and the Pamban Sea Bridge in the same riding day.

dayByDay.note: 140 continuous hairpin bends up and down Kolli Malai in a single relentless session before continuing south toward Rameshwaram.

lessons: Look through the turn, trust the front tyre grip, use 2nd-gear engine braking on the descent to save the brakes, and give wide clearance to TNSTC buses on blind switchbacks.

rides.title: Bangalore to Rameshwaram & Return
rides.summary: Southern coastal expedition across Tamil Nadu through Madurai to Pamban Sea Bridge and the ruins of Dhanushkodi, returning to Bangalore.
rides.story: Riding down to the edge of the subcontinent where the Indian Ocean meets the Bay of Bengal at Dhanushkodi.
highlights: Crossing the iconic Pamban Sea Bridge on two wheels.
Riding to the last road in India at Dhanushkodi.
lessons: Coastal crosswinds require steady throttle and relaxed handlebar grip.

rides.title: Patna to Bangalore
rides.summary: Solo cross-country ride slicing across the heart of the subcontinent: from Patna through Madhya Pradesh, Nagpur, and Hyderabad into Bangalore.
rides.story: Crossing 5 states southwards across central India, traversing the Deccan plateau into Bangalore.
highlights: Transversing the heart of India from Gangetic plains to Deccan plateau.
Navigating the Hyderabad Outer Ring Road corridor.
lessons: Managing long 700+ km highway days with scheduled hydration intervals.

rides.title: Delhi to Patna (Ladakh Return Leg)
rides.summary: The return sprint heading east from Delhi across the northern plains back to Patna basecamp, concluding the Ladakh expedition.
rides.story: Wrapping up the trans-Himalayan expedition with a direct highway sprint from Delhi back home to Patna.
highlights: Grand return to home basecamp in Patna after completing Ladakh.
lessons: Post-Himalayan bike servicing and chain tension adjustment.

rides.title: Delhi to Ladakh Circuit & Return
rides.destination: Leh, Ladakh (Khardung La & Pangong Tso) & Return to Delhi
rides.summary: The main high-altitude circuit: Delhi across Punjab and Jammu & Kashmir into Zoji La, Kargil, Leh, Khardung La summit at 17,590 ft, and Pangong Tso, returning to Delhi.
rides.story: Ascending from sea-level plains into the great high-altitude mountain deserts of Ladakh. Crossing Khardung La at 17,590 ft and the shores of Pangong Tso.
highlights: Conquered Khardung La Pass at 17,590 ft.
Camped at Pangong Tso at 14,270 ft altitude.
lessons: Acclimatization and electrolyte hydration are vital at 15,000+ ft.

rides.title: Patna to Delhi (Ladakh Leg 1)
rides.summary: First leg of the trans-Himalayan expedition. Express highway run across Uttar Pradesh from Patna to Delhi.
rides.story: Expedition flag-off from Patna heading west across Varanasi, Lucknow, and Agra into New Delhi preparing for the Himalayan ascent.
highlights: Expedition flag-off from Patna home basecamp.
Cruising the Purvanchal and Yamuna Expressways.
lessons: Early morning start essential to beat northern highway fog and congestion.

bikeDetails.name: Royal Enfield Meteor 350
bikeDetails.model: Meteor 350 Stellar Edition (Stellar Black Touring Rig)
bikeDetails.engine: 349cc Single Cylinder, 4-stroke, Air-Oil Cooled SOHC J-Series Engine
bikeDetails.rangeKm: ~480 km per tank (32-35 km/L highway touring)

bikeDetails.tagline: The Highway Cruiser Built for Mountain Passes & Ocean Highways
bikeDetails.description: My primary solo expedition steed. Built on Royal Enfield's twin downtube spine frame with counterbalanced J-series single-cylinder thumper, finished in Stellar Black with chrome 3D tank badging and configured with heavy-duty alpine touring armor.
whyThisBike: Low Center of Gravity & 765mm Seat Height: Enables full-foot plant control during treacherous slush, loose scree, and icy gravel hairpins in Ladakh.
Tractor Low-End Thump (27 Nm @ 4,000 RPM): Seamless hill-climbing without frequent gear hunting on 17,500 ft Himalayan switchbacks.
480 km Realistic Fuel Range: 15L teardrop tank essential for crossing remote fuel-dry stretches like the 365 km stretch between Tandi and Karu in Ladakh.
Counterbalanced J-Series Engine: Eliminates high-rpm handlebar buzz, enabling fatigue-free 600+ km daily endurance touring.
Rock-solid Mechanical Reliability: Zero engine breakdown or mechanical drop across 15,480 km of solo cross-country touring.

plannedRides.title: Spiti Valley & Sach Pass Circuit
plannedRides.summary: Tackling the most treacherous cliff-carved mountain roads on earth: Hindustan-Tibet Highway, high-altitude desert of Kaza, Kunzum La, and the notorious Sach Pass cliff-hangers.
plannedRides.description: A high-risk, high-reward trans-Himalayan circuit that tests motorcycle clearance, water-crossing navigation, and high-altitude solo endurance. Entering through Shimla and the Kinnaur gorge, ascending to Tabo and Key Monastery at 12,000 ft, traversing Kunzum Pass (14,931 ft), and descending through the sheer rock walls of Sach Pass (14,482 ft) in Pangi Valley.
highlights: Navigating the sheer cliff-cut corridors of the Hindustan-Tibet highway.
Summiting Kunzum La (14,931 ft) and camping near the Chandratal glacial crescent.
Conquering Sach Pass (14,482 ft) — known as India's most treacherous single-lane mountain road.
Field testing cold-weather engine thermal management and air filtration in Spiti desert dust.

checkpoints.note: Cliff corridors alongside the roaring Satluj river.
High-altitude desert base camp & monastery plateaus.
High mountain pass linking Spiti to Lahaul.

preparationList.task: Royal Enfield Meteor 350 heavy-duty sump bash plate installed
Auxiliary high-penetration amber fog illumination wired
Inner-line permits & Pangi Valley road status monitoring
Satellite SOS beacon & high-altitude emergency oxygen canister

plannedRides.title: Bhutan & Eastern Himalayas Expedition
plannedRides.destination: Thimphu, Paro & Chele La (Kingdom of Bhutan)
plannedRides.summary: Cross-border expedition from Patna across the Dooars tea gardens into the Kingdom of Bhutan, ascending to Chele La Pass at 13,084 ft.
plannedRides.description: An international motorcycle journey threading through North Bengal tea country to Phuentsholing, climbing into the mystical fortress valleys of Thimphu and Paro, and ascending the highest motorable road in Bhutan at Chele La with panoramas of Mt. Jomolhari.
highlights: International overland border crossing at Phuentsholing on two wheels.
Riding the immaculate winding alpine curves through Thimphu and Punakha Dzongs.
Summiting Chele La Pass at 13,084 ft overlooking the sacred Himalayan snow peaks.
Experiencing Bhutan's Carbon-Negative roads and preservation-first mountain ethos.

checkpoints.note: Tea garden highways at the foothills.
Highest motorable mountain pass in Bhutan.

preparationList.task: Overland motorcycle international entry permit documentation
Route mapping across Paro, Punakha, and Dochula Pass
Mandatory local licensed motorcycle guide coordination
Cold-weather rain gear and high-altitude thermal loadout

coverLetter.subject: Application for Full Stack & Systems Engineer
paragraphs: I am writing to express my strong interest in joining your engineering organization as a Full Stack & Systems Engineer. With extensive hands-on experience engineering production systems across Next.js and Go microservices—most prominently architecting a zero-trust enterprise AI orchestrator coordinating 600+ microservice endpoints—I specialize in building performant, fault-tolerant architectures that bridge complex distributed backends with intuitive, high-density user interfaces.

At Fountane, I led the core technical architecture of our enterprise AI orchestrator in Go. Rather than relying on fragile prompt engineering, I engineered a high-concurrency tool routing runtime that parses natural-language queries into parallelized API operations across 600+ microservice endpoints with sub-100ms dispatch latency. Security is enforced as a strict architectural invariant: by forwarding caller-scoped session tokens (JWTs) and programmatically injecting tenant IDs in Go, we eliminated prompt-based tenant drift with 99.9% tenant isolation compliance. Additionally, I designed an autonomous routine runtime for scheduled and event-driven business workflows with human-in-the-loop approvals, reducing operational manual inquiry handling by over 60%.

Complementing my systems work, I engineer responsive web applications using Next.js 15, TypeScript, and React, optimizing rendering lifecycles to reduce page load times by 40% on datasets exceeding 10,000+ records. On the backend tier, I design Go microservices backed by PostgreSQL and MySQL, guaranteeing strict transactional consistency (ACID), automated webhook verification for payment gateways, and dynamic role-based authorization (RBAC). I maintain 85%+ Vitest test coverage on critical business workflows and manage automated GitLab CI/CD release pipelines to ensure reliable, zero-downtime deployments.

I approach engineering with high ownership, deep analytical rigor, and a commitment to measurable outcomes—the same discipline that fuels my solo motorcycle endurance expeditions across thousands of kilometers through Ladakh and Rameshwaram. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my systems mindset, Go microservice expertise, and full-stack execution can make an immediate and lasting contribution to your team.
